items.title: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
items.summary: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?
items.t: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation

items.title: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – Europe live
items.summary:
German chancellor, in wide-ranging speech, says Moscow is ‘escalating on a massive scale’

If you want to hear more about the new death toll, listen to today’s Today in Focus podcast with our Russia expert, Pjotr Sauer.

“Two groups of hackers accessed Russia’s main statistics database last month and discovered a cache of 11m death certificates that revealed nearly 500,000 Russian losses in Ukraine since 2022. Among these were 1,000 – the equivalent of a whole regiment – who took their own lives.

The documents show how the majority of soldiers come from poorer areas and ethnic minorities, drawn in by high salaries. There are also recruits from abroad and even those lured to Russia by offers of jobs. But for how long can Vladimir Putin keep this shocking death toll from the Russian people?”

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – Europe live

items.title: Brits are having less sex, but watching a lot of porn, survey finds
items.summary: A third of Brits aged 16 to 24 have never had sex, a landmark survey finds, though most acknowledge sexting and watching pornography.
items.t: Brits are having less sex, but watching a lot of porn, survey finds

items.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".
items.t: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war

items.title: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president
items.summary: The Mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard, has been re-elected president of the Association of Mayors of France, securing a comfortable victory in a vote announced on Wednesday. Lisnard is also a candidate in next year's French presidential election. For more on what his re-election could mean, FRANCE 24's James André reports from the Association of Mayors' convention in Paris.
items.t: French Mayors Conference: 2027 Elysée hopeful Lisnard reelected association president

items.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.
items.t: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line

items.title: Moldova issues emergency kit guide, prepares citizens for possible expansion of Ukraine war
items.summary: As the war in Ukraine has highlighted the importance of civilian preparedness, Moldova has launched its own emergency readiness programme. Medicine, batteries and three days' worth of food are among the essentials citizens are encouraged to keep at hand, in case they need to leave at a moment's notice.
items.t: Moldova issues emergency kit guide, prepares citizens for possible expansion of Ukraine war

items.title: Exiled Catalan separatist Puigdemont to return to Spain after election
items.summary: Catalan separatist ​and former regional leader Carles Puigdemont said on Wednesday he would end nearly a decade of self-imposed exile in Belgium and return to Spain on December 12, ​after ‌this weekend's national election. Puigdemont, whose legal troubles in ⁠Spain are over after the Supreme Court earlier this week applied an amnesty law to shelve the ‌criminal case against him, said at a televised news conference from ⁠Brussels that he would unveil his proposal for a renewed Catalan independence push on December 17. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.
items.t: Exiled Catalan separatist Puigdemont to return to Spain after election

items.title: 'Paper Tiger': Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver shine in Russian mob thriller
items.summary: This week on arts24, Emma Jones and Dheepthika Laurent discuss the latest film releases. We start with "Paper Tiger", a Russian mob thriller starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller. It is a return to familiar crime thriller territory for James Gray, the director behind "Little Odessa" and "The Yards".
items.t: 'Paper Tiger': Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver shine in Russian mob thriller

items.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
items.summary: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.
items.t: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
items.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

Continue reading...
items.t: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations

items.title: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia
items.summary:
The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

(Image credit: Eddie Raynes)
items.t: How American Thanksgiving took root -- and evolved -- in Liberia

items.title: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Nino
items.summary: Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Nino-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest US travel week of the year. The San Francisco Bay Area is expected to get hit hard with a one-two punch of inclement weather and monster tides, which forecasters warned could push seawater into low-lying areas on Wednesday and Thursday.
items.t: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Nino

items.title: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut
items.summary: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program.
items.t: 'Historic' space mission: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying Pakistani astronaut

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

Continue reading...
items.t: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon

items.title: Aidan is one of thousands of students forced to verbally defend his honours thesis as universities take on AI
items.summary:
Honours students are increasingly being asked to sit oral assessments – but at the University of Sydney it’s become a requirement for all

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When Aidan Elwig Pollock signed up for an honours program at the University of Sydney, he did not expect his 20,000-word thesis to be accompanied by a spoken component.

But, as AI increasingly makes written research an unreliable form of assessment, the university has demanded all students taking the one-year program defend their arguments in conversation with professors.

Continue reading...
items.t: Aidan is one of thousands of students forced to verbally defend his honours thesis as universities take on AI

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, says president
items.summary:
Operation in which one hostage-taker was killed ends daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre, where 30 people were initially held

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

Continue reading...
items.t: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, says president

items.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
items.summary: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The president said that the men were “common criminals” who fled into the supermarket after a failed attempt to hold up an armored truck. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.
items.t: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket

items.title: Large bushfire threatens homes and properties on Flinders Island off Tasmania
items.summary:
Blaze spreads significantly across the north of Flinders Island after being started by lightning strikes

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Homes and properties on a picturesque remote island were under threat on Wednesday night from an out-of-control bushfire that had sent smoke hundreds of kilometres south.

The blaze on Flinders Island in Bass Strait spread significantly on Wednesday after being started by lightning strikes.

items.t: Large bushfire threatens homes and properties on remote island off Tasmania

items.title: Violence against women in the digital age: When the internet becomes a weapon
items.summary: November 25th is the United Nation's International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. In the age of social media and artificial intelligence, there are now new spaces in which violence against women has appeared, with the internet now a growing weapon in the hands of abusers. 85% of women who spend time online have witnessed violence, and 38% have been the target of it.
items.t: Violence against women in the digital age: When the internet becomes a weapon

items.title: Number of women killed by men in Ireland almost doubles in a year
items.summary:
Figures from past 30 years show more than half of victims killed by current or ex-partner

The number of women in Ireland killed by men has surged in the past five years and risen especially sharply in the past 12 months, according to a study.

After falling for two decades, the number of violent deaths began going up in 2021 and has risen sharply this year, with 13 deaths so far, the report by Irish charity Women’s Aid said on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
items.t: Number of women killed by men in Ireland almost doubles in a year

items.title: Why Indian nationals are still ending up in Russia's war on Ukraine
items.summary: Whether through deception or desperation, Indians continue to be drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine. What can New Delhi do to protect its citizens from ending up fighting in Ukraine?
items.t: Why Indian nationals are still ending up in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
items.summary: The US military will on Wednesday detonate some 10,000 pounds of unstable and degraded explosive material in Iowa, where local residents were urged to evacuate amid concerns over possible toxic lead contamination. US officials say the 68 drums of lead azide are at risk of spontaneous explosion. A series of safety measures are being taken to curb potential contamination from the blast, but the Army has encouraged residents of a small town and other nearby areas to leave "out of an abundance of caution."
items.t: US army to detonate stockpile of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa

items.title: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy
items.summary: November 25th is International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. The forgotten victims of femicide are the children who find themselves motherless, often because their mother was killed by their own father. Italy recorded 97 female homicides in 2025 – 62 of them were committed by a partner. These crimes leave whole families devastated and children who have to grow up without their parents. FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Italy, Natalia Mendoza, reports.
items.t: The forgotten victims of femicide: Children orphaned by violence in Italy

items.title: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
items.summary: Iran's U.N. envoy claims the U.S. military used Palantir and Anthropic AI systems to select some 2,000 targets over just four days.
items.t: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI during war

items.title: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack
items.summary: Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.
items.t: Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack

items.title: Producer and guitarist Ginton on jazz, remixing big hits and collaborating on a track for Drake
items.summary: Amsterdam-based guitarist, DJ and music producer Ginton is known for blending reggae, Afro, Caribbean and electronic music. He told FRANCE 24 that his background in jazz was "the reason I can make the music I make today". He also told us of his "surprise" in collaborating on a track for Drake's album "Honestly, Nevermind". He spoke to us in Perspective.

items.title: UK embassy in Japan warns of rise in drink spiking and credit card fraud at Tokyo bars
items.summary:
Social media campaign fronted by British rapper Shao Dow advises tourists not to let their guard down

The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital.

In a recent clip made in conjunction with the embassy, the British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, a frequent visitor to Japan, notes that although the country “is incredibly safe, that doesn’t mean you can let your guard down”.

items.title: ‘A symbol of hope’: Pakistan celebrates as astronaut enters orbit
items.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first Pakistani to reach orbit after blasting off on board a Chinese mission to the country’s Tiangong space station on Tuesday. The Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist’s feat was celebrated by cheers and rapturous applause by those watching in his homeland.
items.t: ‘A symbol of hope’: Pakistan celebrates as astronaut enters orbit

items.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

items.title: Violence against women: Its many forms and the paths to justice
items.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 25: Some 21 percent of women say they have suffered "economic violence", while others are exploring new types of justice for their abusers. In other news, recent leaks on Russian troop losses show 349 deaths in Mali, Russia's biggest military deployment in Africa. items.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".
items.t: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery

items.title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer
items.summary:
Concerns over Beijing’s use of ‘red notices’ as Hong Kong prepares to host police organisation’s general assembly

China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol.

Continue reading...
items.t: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer

items.summary: Climbing tall mountains like Kilimanjaro is a study in contrasts — from beating sun to freezing nights, fire and snow.

items.summary: A recently discovered hack on a CIA analysis system exposed some unclassified information, US media reported on Tuesday. The breach is the latest in a series of cyber attacks that have targeted US government departments and major companies in recent weeks.

Advocates say access to voluntary assisted dying, IVF, elective abortions and gender-affirming care is under threat after the competition watchdog approved the takeover of 14 private hospitals by a Catholic healthcare provider.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) announced on Wednesday it had approved the takeover of the private hospitals by not-for-profit Catholic healthcare operator Calvary from collapsed provider Healthscope.

items.title: ‘You’re protecting Trump’: Hanson-Young clashes with Liberal senator before digital duty of care legislation passes – as it happened
items.summary:
• Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Wells says AI investment and creative protections not a ‘zero-sum game’

Weighing into the gigantic debate that is AI companies wanting to scrape Australian data to train models versus creatives who want to protect their work, Anika Wells says it’s not a ‘zero-sum’ game.

I reject this sort of zero-sum game where building Australian sovereignty in AI must come at the expense of creatives or at diminishing the rights of creatives. At the moment, yes, we want deals, but we want creatives paid properly for their work. And the situation that we find ourselves in at the moment is that they’re not. They have no control and often no payment for their work.

items.title: In charts: how power could shift in Europe’s big year of elections
items.summary:
More than half of EU voters will go to the polls in the next 12 months, with the far right targeting significant gains. We set out the political landscape and trends

Over the coming 12 months, more than half of the EU’s electorate will go to the polls in elections that could change the direction of the continent, with attention focused on voters in four of the bloc’s five biggest states.

In Spain, France and Poland, elections could bring the far right into government. Italy’s far-right prime minister looks likely to remain in power, but is under pressure from a challenger even further to the right.

Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

items.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
items.summary:
WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade

Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

On a visit to Havana, the WHO chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.

Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

items.title: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence
items.summary:
Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran

Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view.

Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geo-strategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race.

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday.

items.title: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
items.summary:
Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship

Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.

Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.

items.title: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack

No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.
